title: Residential roofing catalog for price book setup (US, 2026)
notes: Prices are material cost to a contractor per order unit (bundle, roll, piece, box) unless the item says otherwise. Labor and service items are prices a contractor charges a homeowner.

price_confidence: 'observed' = a public listing was seen (date given); 'sourced_range' = a published cost guide or several listings support the range; 'estimate' = our judgement from related figures. Every default_price is a starting point the organization is expected to replace with its own supplier pricing.
Ids match public/v1/materials/roofing-library-data.ts (lib-*) where the item already exists there; template_item_id names the matching item in public/v1/pricebook/default_template.ts.

Formulas use measurement dictionary keys from public/v1/platform/publication/measurement-schemas.ts (roofing schema v2). Anything that is not a dictionary key is declared in inputs[] with in_dictionary false.
default_markup_note: roofing-library-data.ts sets sell price = base cost x 1.35. Kept here as the suggested starting markup; it is an organization decision, not research.

warranty_system.summary: Every TAMKO shingle carries the Standard Limited Warranty: Limited Lifetime on single-family homes for laminated lines (25-yr for Elite Glass-Seal), with a 10-year Full Start non-prorated period (5 for Elite Glass-Seal). TAMKO Edge Pro Certified contractors can register enhanced limited system warranties on Titan XT and StormFighter FLEX. Shield ($3/SSQ) gives a 20-yr Full Start period. ProShield ($5/SSQ) gives 50 years. MasterShield ($7/SSQ) adds 50 years plus 10-yr workmanship. DiamondShield ($11/SSQ) adds 50 years plus 25-yr workmanship. Shield and ProShield need 3 TAMKO accessories; MasterShield and DiamondShield need 4. Higher tiers need higher certification levels. Separately, the 160 mph WindGUARD wind warranty on Titan XT, StormFighter FLEX and HailGuard needs TAMKO starter plus TAMKO hip & ridge. HailGuard has its own HailGuard Limited System Warranty for hail leaks (hail up to 3 in, up to 20 yrs) and needs a qualifying TAMKO Complete system.

The brochure does not list which accessory categories qualify. TAMKO's accessory families are underlayments, self-adhering underlayments, starter/hip & ridge and ventilation (CoolRidge), so the role list is inferred. WindGUARD 160 mph always needs starter + hip_ridge.

estimating_rules.label: Squares that get shingles
estimating_rules.explanation: A square is 100 square feet of roof. Shingles are not allowed on roof that is nearly flat (2/12 or lower), so those squares are left out and priced as a flat roof.
estimating_rules.note: The price book template uses a key named shingleSquares, which is not in the measurement dictionary; this expression is the dictionary equivalent.

estimating_rules.label: Waste
estimating_rules.explanation: Shingles get cut at every hip, valley and edge, so you buy more than the roof's area. A simple gable roof needs about 10% extra; a hip roof about 15%; a cut-up roof with many valleys and dormers 18-20%.

complexity_hint.note: Our heuristic for suggesting a waste figure from the measurements; not a published rule. Applies only to the field shingles, never to starter, ridge cap or flashing.

estimating_rules.label: Shingle bundles
estimating_rules.explanation: Most shingles come 3 bundles to a square. Heavier designer shingles come 4 or 5 to a square. We take the shingle squares, add waste, and multiply by the bundles per square of the shingle you picked.
estimating_rules.worked_example: 25 shingle squares, 12% waste, 3 bundles per square: 25 x 1.12 x 3 = 84 bundles.

estimating_rules.label: Starter strip
estimating_rules.explanation: Starter strip is the first row along the bottom edges (eaves) and the sloped side edges (rakes). It seals the first course down so wind can't lift it. Manufacturers want it on both edges for their higher wind warranties.
estimating_rules.worked_example: 150 ft of eaves + 90 ft of rakes = 240 lf; with GAF Pro-Start at 120 lf a bundle that is 2 bundles.

estimating_rules.label: Hip and ridge cap
estimating_rules.explanation: The peaks (ridges) and the sloped corners (hips) are covered with special cap shingles. Add the ridge and hip lengths and divide by how many feet one bundle covers.

order_packaging.units_per_package: accessory.coverage.lf (Seal-A-Ridge 25, TimberTex 20, ProEdge 33, RidgeFlex 12 in 30.9, Shadow Ridge 30)

estimating_rules.label: Ice and water barrier
estimating_rules.explanation: A sticky waterproof membrane goes where water and ice back up: along the eaves, down every valley, and over any low-slope section (2/12 to 4/12). In cold climates building code wants it from the eave to 24 inches inside the wall, which usually means two 3-foot rows; in warm climates one row or none.

order_packaging.units_per_package: accessory.coverage.sq_ft_gross / 100, about 1.85 net squares for a 200 sq ft roll after laps (estimate)

estimating_rules.note: The price book template's current LEAK_BARRIER_FORMULA counts one foot per lf of eaves, rakes and valleys ((valleyLf + eavesLf + rakesLf) / 100 + pitch2to4Squares); that understates eave coverage and adds rakes, which most roofers do not cover. Side walls and chimneys may also get a strip; add them per company practice.

estimating_rules.label: Underlayment
estimating_rules.explanation: Synthetic underlayment covers the whole deck under the shingles. A roll covers 10 squares before overlaps; after overlaps, plan on about 9.4 squares a roll.

order_packaging.note: CertainTeed publishes 937.5 sq ft net per 1,000 sq ft roll; use the same for other 10-square rolls unless the manufacturer says otherwise. Many roofers do not subtract the area under ice & water; keeping it is conservative.

estimating_rules.label: Drip edge
estimating_rules.explanation: Metal edge trim goes along the eaves and rakes so water drips clear of the fascia. It comes in 10-foot pieces; we add 5% for overlaps and cuts.

estimating_rules.label: Ridge vent
estimating_rules.explanation: If the house is vented at the ridge, vent runs along the ridges (not the hips). Ridge cap goes over it. Most vents come in 4-foot pieces.
estimating_rules.note: Vent usually stops short of each ridge end; ventilation sizing (1 sq ft of net free area per 150 or 300 sq ft of attic) is a separate check that needs attic area, which the dictionary does not carry (ventilationSquares is the nearest key).

estimating_rules.label: Step flashing
estimating_rules.explanation: Where a roof runs up beside a wall or chimney, one bent metal piece goes under every row of shingles. Rows are about 5 to 5-5/8 inches apart, so it is a little over 2 pieces per foot of wall.
estimating_rules.note: The template prices step flashing per lf of sideWallLf; this expresses pieces. 5.625 in is the exposure of the laminates above (use 5 for 3-tab).

estimating_rules.label: Head wall and apron flashing
estimating_rules.explanation: Where the roof runs into a wall across its top, or along the low side of a chimney, a continuous metal flashing is bent in. Sold in 10-foot pieces.

estimating_rules.label: Valley metal (open valleys only)
estimating_rules.explanation: Some roofers line valleys with metal instead of weaving or cutting shingles. Only add it if you build open valleys.

estimating_rules.label: Coil roofing nails
estimating_rules.explanation: A laminate shingle takes 4 nails (6 in high-wind areas or steep roofs), about 64-66 shingles a square, plus starter and ridge cap. That is roughly 320 nails a square with 4 nails, 450 with 6. A box of 7,200 does about 20 squares, or 15 with 6 nails.

order_packaging.note: squares per 7,200 box at 320 nails per square; use 16 for six-nail installs

estimating_rules.confidence: estimate (the allowance for starter and ridge nails)

estimating_rules.label: Cap nails for underlayment
estimating_rules.explanation: Synthetic underlayment is held down with plastic-cap nails, roughly 150 to 300 a square by the maker's pattern. A pail of about 3,000 does about 20 squares at the lighter pattern, which holds it until the shingles go on.

order_packaging.note: squares per pail of about 3,000 at 150 caps per square; use 10 to fasten to the full pattern

estimating_rules.label: Sealant
estimating_rules.explanation: Tubes of sealant for flashings, vents and ridge ends. Roughly one tube for every 8 squares plus one per pipe boot.

estimating_rules.label: Pipe boots
estimating_rules.explanation: Every plumbing vent pipe through the roof gets a new rubber boot. Count them on the roof report.
estimating_rules.note: Gap: pipe boot count is not a measurement dictionary key, so it cannot be a price book formula token yet. Add a dictionary definition (e.g. roof.pipe_boot_count) before wiring this.

estimating_rules.label: Decking replacement allowance
estimating_rules.explanation: You can't see rotten decking until the old roof is off. Most contracts include a few sheets and charge per sheet after that.

estimating_rules.label: Tear-off
estimating_rules.explanation: Removing the old roof is charged on the whole roof area, one layer at a time.

estimating_rules.label: Extra layers
estimating_rules.explanation: Each extra layer of old shingles under the top one adds more work and more weight to haul away.

estimating_rules.label: Install labor
estimating_rules.explanation: Labor is charged on the roof's real area, without waste. Steeper roofs add a charge on the steep squares only.

estimating_rules.label: Steep charge: 7/12 and 8/12
estimating_rules.explanation: At 7/12 and 8/12 roofers need roof jacks and harnesses and move slower. Charged on those squares only.
estimating_rules.note: The dictionary band is 'over 6/12 up to 8/12', i.e. 7/12 and 8/12 (and fractional pitches between). A company that starts steep charges at 8/12 can use pitch8Squares (exact pitch key) instead.

estimating_rules.label: Steep charge: 9/12 to 12/12
estimating_rules.explanation: Above 8/12 you can't walk the roof; everything is done from roof jacks. Charged on those squares only.
estimating_rules.note: Xactimate splits steep charges at 7-9/12 and 10-12/12; the dictionary bands split at 8/12. Exact pitch keys (pitch9Squares, pitch10Squares, ...) can rebuild Xactimate tiers if a company needs them.

estimating_rules.label: Steep charge: steeper than 12/12
estimating_rules.explanation: Very steep sections (mansards, towers) are slow, careful work. Charged on those squares only.

estimating_rules.label: High roof (2 stories or more)
estimating_rules.explanation: Two-story roofs take longer to load and need more fall protection.
estimating_rules.note: Gap: stories is not in the dictionary and price book formulas have no comparison operator.

estimating_rules.label: Hand-carry
estimating_rules.explanation: When the truck can't load the roof directly, shingles go up and debris comes down by hand.

estimating_rules.label: Dumpster
estimating_rules.explanation: Old shingles weigh about 250-350 lb a square. One 20-yard dumpster usually takes about 30 squares of a single layer.

estimating_rules.label: Permit
estimating_rules.explanation: One permit per job where the city or county requires it.

estimating_rules.label: Intake vent
estimating_rules.explanation: Continuous intake runs along the eaves, so air drawn in low leaves at the ridge. Most intake vents come in 4-foot pieces.
estimating_rules.provisional_note: Provisional (2026-10-25): full eave length is a starting point; balanced ventilation sizing needs attic area, which the dictionary does not carry.

estimating_rules.label: Box vents
estimating_rules.explanation: Static vents are counted on the roof, which the measurement report does not do, so they are entered on each job.
estimating_rules.provisional_note: Entered by hand: the dictionary has no vent count.

regions.label: Northeast
regions.basis: sourced_range for labor (Roofing Brief editorial +20-30% for NY/MA/CT/NJ, +5-15% for PA; RSMeans-based labor $2.25-3.00/sq ft vs $1.75-2.25 Midwest); material_multiplier is an estimate

regions.label: South
regions.basis: sourced_range (Roofing Brief: Sun Belt = national baseline; EstimatorSuite Southeast 0.90x; RSMeans-based labor lowest of the regions). Florida is an exception: +15-25%, Miami-Dade/Broward HVHZ +30-50%.

regions.label: Mountain West and Southwest
regions.basis: sourced_range for labor (Roofing Brief: national to +5% for CO/UT/ID/MT/WY; EstimatorSuite Southwest 1.10x); material_multiplier is an estimate

regions.label: Pacific
regions.basis: sourced_range for labor (Roofing Brief: WA/OR +10-20%, CA +25-40%; EstimatorSuite West Coast 1.40x; RoofVista +10-20%); material_multiplier is an estimate; AK and HI are higher still and not covered by any source

regions_note: Regional multipliers come from cost guides about installed cost, which is mostly labor. Material (supplier) prices vary far less by region than by supplier, volume and freight, so material_multiplier stays near 1.0 and is an estimate. price_multiplier equals labor_multiplier and is what the setup flow should apply to labor and service items; apply material_multiplier to materials only if the organization has no supplier prices.

market_notes.text: Shingle makers announced two rounds of increases in 2026: up to about 8% effective late March to mid-April (CertainTeed, GAF, Owens Corning, Atlas, Malarkey; TAMKO 4-5%) and 6-9% effective June 1 (GAF, Owens Corning, IKO). Roughly 10-16% year over year for architectural bundles entering Q2 2026.
Section 232 steel and aluminum duties rose to 50% in April 2026; Gibraltar announced 10-13% on aluminum trim and flashing, which affects drip edge, step flashing and valley metal.
